docs.text: Silverlight360.Https ¶ HTTP and HTTPS from a Silverlight360 app on the Xbox 360, with TLS 1.2 and 1.3. It's libcurl 8.23 on Mbed TLS 3.6.7, the xsdk ports curl-xenon and mbedtls-xenon , built into a DLL of its own, https360.xex , which an app calls from C# through HttpsClient . using (var client = new HttpsClient()) // checks servers against game:\cacert.pem { // On a thread of its own: requests block until the response is in. HttpsResponse page = client.Get("https://example.com/"); HttpsResponse posted = client.Post("https://api.example.com/items", "application/json", Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("{\"name\": \"xbox\"}")); client.Download("https://example.com/big.zip", @"hdd:\Downloads\big.zip", true); } The platform's own HttpWebRequest does HTTPS too, but only with the certificate authorities the console knows, which are years old: it can't reach example.com or github.com , for instance. Silverlight360.Https brings Mozilla's current roots and TLS 1.3, and its requests run on any thread, not the UI's. Its drop-in, HttpsRequestCreator.Register() , sends an app's existing WebClient and HttpWebRequest calls through it (see Adding it to an app ). Getting it ¶ A release has what an app needs, built: https360.xex The DLL, at base 0x8D000000 cacert.pem Mozilla's root certificates, which servers are checked against Silverlight360.Https.dll , Silverlight360.Https.xml The C# side, with its documentation for IntelliSense: HttpsClient , and the drop-in for the platform's WebClient and HttpWebRequest . It needs Silverlight360.Common, which an app built with Silverlight360 has licenses/ , THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md curl's, Mbed TLS's and Mozilla's licenses, which go with the DLL LICENSE.md , README.md , BUILD.txt Silverlight360.Https's license, and what the release was built from Then see Adding it to an app . To build it yourself, see Building . Why curl on Mbed TLS ¶ Already ported for the console. xsdk's own ports, built on its sockets, getaddrinfo , getentropy and clocks, and checked on a real console: Mbed TLS's self-tests, TLS 1.2 to public hosts, and 9 MB/s downloads over ChaCha20-Poly1305. Modern TLS. Mbed TLS 3.6 is an LTS release with TLS 1.3. mbedtls-xenon builds TLS 1.2 only by default; config/mbedtls.h keeps 1.3 in. A real HTTP client. curl brings redirects, chunked transfers, keep-alive, timeouts, Range resumes and certificate name checks, none of which an app has to write itself. Fast on the console's CPU. Mbed TLS offers ChaCha20-Poly1305 first, which ran about four times faster than AES-GCM on the console, and servers that weigh the client's order take it. Licenses an app can ship. curl's license is MIT-style and Mbed TLS's is Apache 2.0. BearSSL has no TLS 1.3, wolfSSL is GPL unless bought, and OpenSSL is several times larger, with no xsdk port. Where it runs ¶ On a console (retail kernel 2.0.17559, running unsigned code) inside Silverdash360 , and in xenia-edge . See Testing for what was checked where.

docs.text: API ¶ Silverlight360.Https.dll ( csharp/HttpsClient.cs ), namespace Silverlight360.Https . HttpsClient ¶ new HttpsClient() A client checking servers against game:\cacert.pem new HttpsClient(string caFile) A client checking servers against the PEM root certificates in caFile HttpsResponse Get(string url) A GET, its whole body in memory HttpsResponse Post(string url, string contentType, byte[] body) A POST HttpsResponse Send(string method, string url, string[] headers, byte[] body) Any method; headers are "Name: value" lines, body may be null HttpsResponse Download(string url, string path, bool resume) A GET written straight to a file on the console's drives, such as hdd:\Downloads\a.zip , with no size limit; its Body is null void Resolve(string entry) Sends a host and port to another address for every request after, as "localhost:7381:192.168.0.125" ; the certificate is still checked against the name void Cancel() From another thread: stops the request at its next block of data, which then throws HttpsException with Cancelled long BytesReceived , long BytesTotal From another thread: the body's bytes so far (a resumed download's first part among them), and its whole size, -1 until the server says void Dispose() Closes the client's connections Settings, for the requests after they're set: FollowRedirects Follows 3xx responses' Location , up to 10 times; on unless set TimeoutSeconds The longest a request may take; 0, no limit, unless set ConnectTimeoutSeconds The longest a connection may take to open, name lookup and handshake included; 30 unless set MaxResponseBytes The largest body kept in memory; 0 for the DLL's 64 MB. Download has no limit Insecure Skips certificate and name checks: for a test server only Verbose Writes curl's trace of each request to the log, default.log in game:\ where it can be written, and to DbgPrint The DLL, for all clients: static void Start(uint heapBytes) Starts the DLL with a heap of up to heapBytes , reserved now and committed as it's used; once, and the first client does it with DefaultHeapBytes if nothing has static uint Version The wrapper's API version, then curl's, 16 bits each: 0x00010817 for curl 8.23 static uint HeapCommitted , static uint HeapPeak The DLL's heap in use now, and the most it has held at once: what to size Start by With Download and resume , a file already there is taken as the first part and the rest asked for with Range ; a server that sends the whole file again (200) starts it over. HttpsResponse ¶ int Status The HTTP status, as 200 or 404 string Headers The final response's header lines as they came, its status line first string Header(string name) The first value of a header, its name in any case; null if there's none byte[] Body , string Text The body, and the body as UTF-8; null for a Download string Url The URL the response came from, after redirects string TlsVersion "TLSv1.3" or "TLSv1.2" , empty over HTTP string Cipher Mbed TLS's name for the cipher suite, as "TLS1-3-CHACHA20-POLY1305-SHA256" int Redirects , int ElapsedMilliseconds The redirects followed, and the whole request's time HttpsException ¶ No response came. Code is curl's CURLcode ; the message is curl's. Constant Code CouldNotResolve 6 The name didn't resolve CouldNotConnect 7 Nothing answered at the address WriteError 23 A Download 's file couldn't be written TimedOut 28 TimeoutSeconds or ConnectTimeoutSeconds ran out TlsFailed 35 The TLS handshake failed Cancelled 42 Cancel() TooManyRedirects 47 More than 10 redirects BadCertificate 60 The server's certificate didn't check out The drop-in: HttpsWebRequest ¶ Silverlight360.Https.dll ( csharp/HttpsWebRequest.cs ), namespace Silverlight360.Https . It makes the platform's own WebRequest.Create , HttpWebRequest and WebClient go through Silverlight360.Https, so existing code needs no change: HttpsRequestCreator.Register(); // https://; Register(true) takes http:// too HttpsRequestCreator.Register() , Register(bool http) WebRequest.RegisterPrefix for https:// , and http:// with true ; false if a prefix couldn't be registered. Once, at the app's start: it holds until the app ends HttpsWebRequest : HttpWebRequest Method , Headers , ContentType , Accept , CookieContainer , BeginGetRequestStream / EndGetRequestStream , BeginGetResponse / EndGetResponse and Abort , as the platform's; and MaxResponseBytes and TimeoutSeconds of its own HttpsWebRequest.UserAgent The User-Agent to send, where the request is typed HttpsWebRequest . The platform's HttpWebRequest.UserAgent can't be used on any class but its own: it throws NotImplementedException (its GetUserAgent and SetUserAgent are internal to System.Net ), and Headers won't take a User-Agent HttpsWebRequest.DefaultUserAgent Sent when a request gives none: "Silverlight360.Https" unless set. Some servers, GitHub's API among them, turn away a request without one HttpsWebResponse : HttpWebResponse StatusCode , StatusDescription , Headers (a WebHeaderCollection ), ContentType , ContentLength , ResponseUri (after redirects), Cookies , GetResponseStream() , and TlsVersion As the platform's client stack does: callbacks come on a thread pool thread, and WebClient takes its events to the thread that started it; a status of 400 or more throws a WebException from EndGetResponse with the response in it, its Status UnknownError (this runtime's WebExceptionStatus has no ProtocolError ), so WebClient 's e.Error has it; no response is ConnectFailure , Abort() is RequestCanceled , and a body over MaxResponseBytes is MessageLengthLimitExceeded . Requests share a pool of four clients, so a host's connection stays open from one request to the next. The response is read whole before EndGetResponse returns, whatever AllowReadStreamBuffering says. Credentials ( ICredentials ) aren't sent.

docs.text: Building ¶ The DLL builds in WSL (or on Linux) with xsdk's toolchain. Clone with the submodules, then set up the rest, in PowerShell: git clone --recursive https://github.com/Digiex/Silverlight360.Https.git cd Silverlight360.Https .\tools\Configure.ps1 Configure.ps1 gets what the build needs, each the way that suits it: curl-xenon , mbedtls-xenon Submodules in deps/ , at the commits Silverlight360.Https is built from (Mbed TLS's framework with them) Checked out if a clone wasn't --recursive xsdk jessenic/xsdk , branch dll-modules , the build XboxNGen uses: its elf2xex.py has --dll , and its build/libxsdk.a is what the DLL links Found from -Xsdk , XSDK , XboxNGen's configuration beside this repository, or a checkout two folders up ( C:\Proj\xsdk ) or beside it; otherwise cloned two folders up, if you say so. libxsdk.a is built if it isn't xsdk's toolchain GCC 15.3, binutils and newlib for powerpc-xsdk-elf , in WSL Found in ~/xsdk-gcc or at -Toolchain ; otherwise built there with xsdk's tools/toolchain/build.sh , if you say so: about 10 minutes, and a 136 MB download of their sources Silverlight360 The SDK, for Silverlight360.Https.dll and the sample Found from -Silverlight360 , its environment variable, or a checkout beside this repository; otherwise cloned there, if you say so It also checks WSL has make , cmake , ninja , python3 and git ( sudo apt install build-essential cmake ninja-build python3 git in Debian; xsdk's own docs/GETTING_STARTED.md lists what its toolchain needs besides). -NonInteractive asks nothing: -CloneXsdk , -BuildToolchain and -CloneSilverlight360 say what it may fetch or build. It writes config.mk ( XSDK and TOOLCHAIN as WSL sees them, for the Makefile), config.props (for the sample's project) and config.json (for tools\Release.ps1 ); git ignores them, and -Show prints them. Then, in WSL, in the repository's folder. The first build compiles both libraries, about 300 files: make -j$(nproc) That writes https360.xex (1.7 MB). It also copies in cacert.pem , Mozilla's roots as mbedtls-xenon has them, and test-ca2.crt , Mbed TLS's test CA, for the sample. After changing a port, run cmake --build build/deps and then make ; make clean starts over. The Makefile's XSDK , TOOLCHAIN , ELF2XEX , MBEDTLS_XENON and CURL_XENON can be given on its command line to build with something else. To move a port to a newer commit: check it out in deps/<port> , build and test, and commit the submodule. Silverlight360.Https.dll ¶ The C# side builds as a Silverlight360 class library, in PowerShell: ..\XboxSilverlightSdk\tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 -Project .\csharp\Silverlight360.Https.csproj That writes csharp\bin\Release\Silverlight360.Https.dll and Silverlight360.Https.xml , its documentation for IntelliSense, with Silverlight360.Common.dll , which it references, beside them. The sample ¶ sample/ is a Silverlight360 app that runs 31 checks against a local server and public hosts. In PowerShell, with Silverlight360 where .\tools\Configure.ps1 -Show says (here beside this repository, as XboxSilverlightSdk ): ..\XboxSilverlightSdk\tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 -Project .\sample\HttpsSample.csproj See Testing for running it.

docs.text: Contributing ¶ Bug reports, fixes and improvements are welcome on GitHub . Say what you're changing in an issue first if it's more than a small fix, so the work isn't done twice. Clone with --recursive , run .\tools\Configure.ps1 , build it ( Building ) and run the sample's checks in xenia-edge ( Testing ). A change to the DLL's loading, its memory or its network should be tried on a console too, with the DLL probed first. Keep HttpsClient.cs building for Silverlight 3's C# and its own NativeBuffer , and the API in API up to date with what it has. Open a pull request against master . The docs site is built for it, so a broken link shows before the merge. Don't send code or files from the Xbox 360 SDK, or from projects whose licenses don't allow it. License ¶ Silverlight360.Https is licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 with an additional condition. By opening a pull request, you agree that your contribution is licensed under the same terms.

docs.text: Development ¶ What's here ¶ src/https.c The DLL's API on curl's easy interface: clients, requests, responses copied out src/runtime.c The runtime xsdk's title start would set up, set up by https360_init instead, with a bounded heap (from UnRar360) src/export.h , src/runtime.h HTTPS360_EXPORT , which gives a function an ordinal for elf2xex, and the runtime's interface config/mbedtls.h Mbed TLS's configuration: the default, TLS 1.3 kept deps/curl-xenon , deps/mbedtls-xenon The two ports, as submodules deps/CMakeLists.txt Builds them as static libraries https360.ld , Makefile The DLL's layout, at base 0x8D000000 , and its build csharp/HttpsClient.cs , csharp/HttpsWebRequest.cs The C# side: HttpsClient , HttpsResponse , HttpsException , and the drop-in csharp/Silverlight360.Https.csproj Builds them as Silverlight360.Https.dll , a Silverlight360 class library, with its XML documentation sample/ A Silverlight360 app that runs 31 checks against a local server and public hosts tests/ The local HTTPS server, and a check of what the sample downloaded tools/Configure.ps1 , tools/Config.ps1 Sets up the build ( Building ), and reads what it saved tools/Release.ps1 Builds a release and publishes it on GitHub docs/ , mkdocs.yml This site The C side and the C# side share the layout of a transfer ( Transfer in src/https.c , 672 bytes, which a static assert holds to, and the offsets at the top of HttpsClient.cs ), big-endian; a change to one is a change to both. The exports are by ordinal, #1 to #9 : the HTTPS360_EXPORT lines in src/https.c , and the DllImport s. Releasing ¶ .\tools\Release.ps1 -DryRun # builds and zips, shows the notes, publishes nothing .\tools\Release.ps1 # 0.1.0 first, then the last release's patch raised .\tools\Release.ps1 -Bump Minor As Silverdash360's and XboxNGen's release scripts do: The release is made from the commit as it is: nothing may be uncommitted, and the commit must be on GitHub already. Nothing is pushed. The version is -Version if given, else the last release's (the highest v<version> tag) with its patch, or -Bump 's part, raised. It's tagged v<version> on the commit, by gh . The DLL is built from scratch in WSL ( make clean , then make ), with what tools\Configure.ps1 set up, and the submodules at the commits this one records. Silverlight360.Https.dll and Silverlight360.Https.xml are built from csharp\Silverlight360.Https.csproj by Silverlight360's tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 , so a release needs Silverlight360 configured. Silverlight360.Https-<version>.zip , in build\release , has in a Silverlight360.Https folder https360.xex , cacert.pem , Silverlight360.Https.dll , Silverlight360.Https.xml , README.md , LICENSE.md , THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md , licenses\ and BUILD.txt , which records the commits of Silverlight360.Https, the two ports and xsdk it was built from, and the toolchain. The release's notes are the commits since the last release, and the zip is its file. It needs the GitHub CLI ( gh ), signed in, unless -DryRun . Test a build before releasing it ( Testing ): the script builds it, it doesn't run it. The docs ¶ This site is the docs folder, built with MkDocs ( mkdocs.yml ). A push to master that changes it publishes it to GitHub Pages ( .github/workflows/docs.yml ). To preview it: pip install mkdocs==1.6.1 python -m mkdocs serve

docs.text: src/https.c The DLL's API on curl's easy interface: clients, requests, responses copied out src/runtime.c The runtime xsdk's title start would set up, set up by https360_init instead, with a bounded heap (from UnRar360) src/export.h , src/runtime.h HTTPS360_EXPORT , which gives a function an ordinal for elf2xex, and the runtime's interface config/mbedtls.h Mbed TLS's configuration: the default, TLS 1.3 kept deps/curl-xenon , deps/mbedtls-xenon The two ports, as submodules deps/CMakeLists.txt Builds them as static libraries https360.ld , Makefile The DLL's layout, at base 0x8D000000 , and its build csharp/HttpsClient.cs , csharp/HttpsWebRequest.cs The C# side: HttpsClient , HttpsResponse , HttpsException , and the drop-in csharp/Silverlight360.Https.csproj Builds them as Silverlight360.Https.dll , a Silverlight360 class library, with its XML documentation sample/ A Silverlight360 app that runs 31 checks against a local server and public hosts tests/ The local HTTPS server, and a check of what the sample downloaded tools/Configure.ps1 , tools/Config.ps1 Sets up the build ( Building ), and reads what it saved tools/Release.ps1 Builds a release and publishes it on GitHub docs/ , mkdocs.yml This site The C side and the C# side share the layout of a transfer ( Transfer in src/https.c , 672 bytes, which a static assert holds to, and the offsets at the top of HttpsClient.cs ), big-endian; a change to one is a change to both. The exports are by ordinal, #1 to #9 : the HTTPS360_EXPORT lines in src/https.c , and the DllImport s.

docs.text: .\tools\Release.ps1 -DryRun # builds and zips, shows the notes, publishes nothing .\tools\Release.ps1 # 0.1.0 first, then the last release's patch raised .\tools\Release.ps1 -Bump Minor As Silverdash360's and XboxNGen's release scripts do: The release is made from the commit as it is: nothing may be uncommitted, and the commit must be on GitHub already. Nothing is pushed. The version is -Version if given, else the last release's (the highest v<version> tag) with its patch, or -Bump 's part, raised. It's tagged v<version> on the commit, by gh . The DLL is built from scratch in WSL ( make clean , then make ), with what tools\Configure.ps1 set up, and the submodules at the commits this one records. Silverlight360.Https.dll and Silverlight360.Https.xml are built from csharp\Silverlight360.Https.csproj by Silverlight360's tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 , so a release needs Silverlight360 configured. Silverlight360.Https-<version>.zip , in build\release , has in a Silverlight360.Https folder https360.xex , cacert.pem , Silverlight360.Https.dll , Silverlight360.Https.xml , README.md , LICENSE.md , THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md , licenses\ and BUILD.txt , which records the commits of Silverlight360.Https, the two ports and xsdk it was built from, and the toolchain. The release's notes are the commits since the last release, and the zip is its file. It needs the GitHub CLI ( gh ), signed in, unless -DryRun . Test a build before releasing it ( Testing ): the script builds it, it doesn't run it.

docs.text: Limits ¶ IPv4, HTTP/1.1. No HTTP/2 or 3, IPv6, proxies, cookies or compressed transfers. Send Accept-Encoding only for something you will decode yourself. ANSI strings. URLs, headers and paths go to the DLL as single-byte strings, so encode anything outside ASCII in the URL yourself. Every new connection reads cacert.pem again, 121 roots in 189 KB. Connections that are kept open don't. A fatal error in the DLL (an abort ) stops the request's thread for good rather than the app, as in UnRar360. The log says why. The log is the host title's, default.log in game:\ , where game: can be written. Under xenia-edge it can't be, so Verbose mirrors to DbgPrint. xenia-edge's random numbers repeat: its XeCryptRandom returns the same bytes on every run, so keys made there aren't secret. The console's are random (mbedtls-xenon's notes). The network's buffers. xsdk_network_limits in src/https.c raises the socket buffers only if the DLL starts the network first. In an app, the runtime has started it already, so the console's defaults apply; requests worked with them on a console, and no download speed has been measured there yet. One base address. The DLL is linked at 0x8D000000 , one of the bases free in a Silverlight app's process on the console; another DLL in the same app needs another.

docs.text: Testing ¶ In xenia-edge ¶ New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $env:TEMP\https-content\HttpsTest Start-Process python -ArgumentList '-I', 'tests\https_server.py', '--seconds', '600' ..\XboxSilverlightSdk\tools\Test-XboxApp.ps1 -Xex .\sample\bin\Release\xbox\default.xex -Output $env:TEMP\https-run ` -ExtraArgs "--content_root=$env:TEMP\https-content" -Seconds 150 python tests\verify_downloads.py $env:TEMP\https-content\HttpsTest tests/https_server.py serves HTTPS on 7443, with TLS 1.2 and 1.3, and on 7444, with TLS 1.2 only. It uses Mbed TLS's test certificate for localhost , from mbedtls-xenon's framework/data_files . The sample sends localhost to 127.0.0.1 with Resolve . On a console, set Server in sample/MainPage.xaml.cs to the PC's address. What passed in xenia-edge, 2026-11-02: all 31 checks; the heap peaked at 1.9 MB. Local: GETs over TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2, their SHA-256 checked; POSTs from 1 KB to 1 MB, echoed back with their hashes, plus PUT, DELETE and HEAD; a redirect followed and one not followed, a 404, and a response over MaxResponseBytes refused; an 8 MB download to hdd: , one cancelled at 2 MB and then resumed with a 206, both byte for byte; a wrong name refused, then accepted with Insecure , and a closed port refused. Public: example.com, www.google.com and api.github.com, over TLS 1.3 with ChaCha20-Poly1305; tls-v1-2.badssl.com over TLS 1.2; expired, wrong-host, self-signed and untrusted-root certificates from badssl.com, each refused for its own reason. Uploads needed a fix in xenia-edge. xenia opens a guest TCP socket as a host acceptor and swaps in a new host socket at connect . That lost the guest's FIONBIO and its options, so a non-blocking socket's recv blocked on the host. A POST larger than one TLS record stalled: curl reads between records, and the read never came back. The fix is in xenia-edge's src/xenia/kernel/xsocket.cc and xsocket.h . It is not a console problem. On a console ¶ Before an app calls a new build, check that the console loads it: a DllImport of a module that can't load turns into a call through null, which can power the console off. The CLR loads a DllImport module as GAME:\<name> with XexLoadImage flags 9; Silverdash360's debug server does the same with xex.probe GAME:\https360.xex 9 , then unloads it. What ran on a console, 2026-11-07, inside Silverdash360 (retail kernel 2.0.17559, running unsigned code): XexLoadImage loaded the DLL at 0x8D000000 (status 0), after the runtime had started the network; GETs to xenia-manager.github.io, raw.githubusercontent.com and api.github.com, over TLS 1.3 with ChaCha20-Poly1305: 170 to 370 ms for the first request to a host, less on a kept connection; a 404 from GitHub Pages, as a response; GitHub's release download, following its redirect to GitHub's file storage, 1.2 MB checked against its SHA-256; the heap peaked at 1.7 MB. Again the same day, the DLL built against xsdk's dll-modules libxsdk.a ( tools\Configure.ps1 's xsdk, the one XboxNGen uses), with the drop-in: Silverdash360 loaded it at its start and fetched its art with it; before HttpsRequestCreator.Register() , the platform's HttpWebRequest failed for example.com and github.com; after it, WebRequest.Create gave HttpsWebRequest s, which got 200 from example.com, github.com (524 KB) and api.github.com; WebClient.DownloadStringAsync got example.com and x360db's info.json , the content type in ResponseHeaders , and a 404 came as e.Error , a WebException with the response, its status 404; WebClient.UploadStringAsync POSTed its body, with its Content-Type , and Accept set on the request arrived, with the default User-Agent .

docs.text: Adding it to an app ¶ An app needs the C# side and two files beside default.xex : Silverlight360.Https.dll , the C# side, HttpsClient and the drop-in, with Silverlight360.Https.xml beside it for IntelliSense: a reference to the release's DLL, or a ProjectReference to the repository's csharp/Silverlight360.Https.csproj . https360.xex and cacert.pem , as Content . The C# side uses NativeBuffer from Silverlight360's common library , Silverlight360.Common, for the memory the DLL reads and writes. An app built with Silverlight360 references that library already, and its build puts Silverlight360.Common.dll in the package. In the app's project, as sample/HttpsSample.csproj has them: <ItemGroup> <ProjectReference Include="..\Silverlight360.Https\csharp\Silverlight360.Https.csproj" /> <!-- or, from a release: <Reference Include="Silverlight360.Https"><HintPath>..\Silverlight360.Https\Silverlight360.Https.dll</HintPath></Reference> --> </ItemGroup> <ItemGroup> <Content Include="..\Silverlight360.Https\https360.xex"><Link>https360.xex</Link></Content> <Content Include="..\Silverlight360.Https\cacert.pem"><Link>cacert.pem</Link></Content> </ItemGroup> Ship the release's licenses folder and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md with them too: curl's and Mbed TLS's licenses ask for their notices to go with the binary. Silverlight360.Https's own license asks for a visible reference to https://github.com/Digiex/Silverlight360.Https in the app's documentation, credits or "about" information (see Licenses ). The drop-in ¶ To leave an app's WebClient and HttpWebRequest code as it is, register the drop-in, in Silverlight360.Https.dll , once, at the start: HttpsRequestCreator.Register(); var web = new WebClient(); web.DownloadStringCompleted += (s, e) => Show(e.Error == null ? e.Result : e.Error.Message); web.DownloadStringAsync(new Uri("https://example.com/")); From then on every https:// request the app makes through the platform goes through Silverlight360.Https, with TLS 1.3 and Mozilla's roots; Register(true) takes http:// too. On a console the platform's own stack fails for example.com and github.com , and Silverlight360.Https's doesn't. See API . What each one has ¶ HttpsClient HttpsWebRequest The platform's HttpWebRequest TLS 1.3, Mozilla's current roots yes yes no: the console's own TLS and roots, which fail for example.com and github.com Works off the UI thread blocks, on any thread Begin / End , on the thread pool yes WebClient no yes yes Request body byte[] a stream a stream Response body in memory, or a file of any size in memory in memory, or read as it comes Response headers lines as they came, Header(name) WebHeaderCollection WebHeaderCollection Cookies no CookieContainer CookieContainer Progress, cancelling BytesReceived , Cancel() Abort() WebClient 's progress events, Abort() Downloads to a file, resumed yes no no Credentials ( ICredentials ) no no yes Compressed responses no no not checked Making requests ¶ Requests block until the response is in, so make them on a thread of their own, never the UI's: ThreadPool.QueueUserWorkItem(delegate { try { using (var client = new HttpsClient { TimeoutSeconds = 30 }) { HttpsResponse response = client.Get("https://api.github.com/"); string text = response.Status == 200 ? response.Text : null; Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(() => Show(text)); } } catch (HttpsException e) { // No response came: e.Code is curl's, such as HttpsException.BadCertificate. } }); One request at a time per client. A client keeps its connections open, so the next request to the same host skips the handshake: 7 ms against 260 ms for the first in xenia-edge. Use one client per thread for requests at the same time. Statuses aren't errors. Any HTTP response comes back as an HttpsResponse , 404 included. HttpsException means no response came. The first client starts the DLL with a heap of DefaultHeapBytes (96 MB, reserved and committed as it's used). Call HttpsClient.Start(bytes) before the first client for another size; HeapPeak says what the requests needed. Silverdash360 gives it 16 MB, and its requests have peaked under 2 MB. The DLL loads at 0x8D000000 . In a Silverlight app's process on the console, 0x8A000000 , 0x8C000000 and 0x8E000000 are taken, so another DLL of the app's can't be at this base. A DllImport of a module that can't load turns into a call through null, which can power the console off, so check a new build loads first (see Testing ). Certificates ¶ Servers are checked against game:\cacert.pem , and against the console's clock, which has to be right. Pass another PEM file to new HttpsClient(path) to trust other roots. Insecure turns the checks off, for a test server only. See API for everything a client has.
